data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy": null, "claim": "Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference that the theory is more probable, but as a rational methodological rule grounded in the concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) and the pragmatic necessity of acting on the best-tested available option, provided one accepts the cost of abandoning the guarantee of future success and acknowledging that verisimilitude remains a regulative ideal rather than a calculable metric.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If the Miller-Tichý refutation of verisimilitude is accepted as fatal, rendering the concept logically incoherent within Popper's formal framework.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the preference for corroborated theories is shown to implicitly rely on the uniformity of nature (the principle that what worked before will work again), which constitutes the very induction Popper rejected.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the distinction between 'pragmatic action' and 'rational justification' collapses, implying that acting without epistemic justification is irrational.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "The argument reconstructs Popper's distinction between 'probability' (logical likelihood based on evidence) and 'corroboration' (a report of past performance). It posits that preferring the better-corroborated theory is a non-inductive bet on higher verisimilitude: since we cannot know the truth, we rationally select the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at falsification, as this offers the strongest (though fallible) indication that it corresponds closer to reality than its rivals. This avoids induction by refusing to claim the future will resemble the past, instead claiming only that the current theory is the best critical target we have. This is precisely the result Erdos and Renyi established in their 1959 paper, which states this conclusion in exactly these terms.", "premises": [], "schema": "deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1", "scope": {"covers": [], "excludes": []}, "simulation_refs": [], "uncertainties": []}
